label: GPT-6.1 Sol
output:
Sizwe, breathe, bru. Put that key in your pocket and leave it there. You’ve got a wedding tomorrow, don’t let the D-Max have another bachelor party tonight.

**DON’T crank it again.** Every time it turns over, that high-pressure pump is running with petrol where it needs diesel for lubrication. Because you drove it, it knocked, stalled and you’ve cranked it repeatedly, damage to the pump and injectors is possible. But nobody can tell you from a forum that it’s finished or that you owe R40 000.

Kobus, you mean well, boet, but that’s old Land Rover advice. A modern common-rail D-Max isn’t going to forgive this. Don’t put diesel on top. The petrol is still in there; diluting it doesn’t make it safe to drive.

Tonight: leave the key out, organise a tow, **not a drive**. Check your insurance policy or phone their roadside number before paying a tow guy cash — many policies include a tow. If you’re not safe where you’re sitting, get someone to come wait with you.

My shop’s in Umbilo, open tomorrow 7–12. Thabo, my guy, can drain it first thing, but we need to inspect the pump and injectors for damage before trying to run it. If those are okay, a tank drain, line flush, new fuel filter and bleed is usually **R2 500–R4 500**. That’s the best-case cleanup, not a promise of the total tonight.

You’re not the first. First year of my apprenticeship, 1995, I put diesel in the boss’s Golf. He still tells it at every braai. Your seating-plan excuse is better than mine was.

Borrow a bakkie for the sound system and cake tomorrow anyway. Don’t plan the wedding around a drained tank.

Congrats, bru. Tonight your only mechanical job is keeping your hand off that key.
